name: AZ-07
label: Safe D

key_factors: D+13 district lean in heavily Democratic AZ-07
Incumbent Grijalva with large fundraising advantage
model.rationale: The district's D+13 lean, Grijalva's incumbency and roughly ten-to-one fundraising edge, and Polymarket pricing the race at 99% Democratic all point to a safe hold. No contrary polling or ratings justify moving off the fundamentals-based margin.
model.watch: Any late polling showing an unusually competitive environment or a surge of outside spending against Grijalva would be the main signal to revisit.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Arizona's 7th District is a heavily Democratic seat, and Adelita Grijalva holds it as an incumbent after winning the nomination. She has raised about $2.3 million and holds over $400,000 on hand, while Republican Daniel Butierez has raised roughly $224,000 with almost no cash remaining and no visible outside support. No independent general-election polls are available, and no expert raters list the race, so the outlook rests on district fundamentals and resources.

Prediction markets price the race at about 99% for Democrats, consistent with the district's D+13 lean and the incumbent's advantages. The forecast expects Grijalva to win comfortably, with a wide but not extreme margin reflecting the absence of direct polling.
